summary: Independently verified the new server-side ABUSE PROTECTION (in-memory sliding-window rate limiter) and alias/callsign profanity filter added this session. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration15_abuse_protection.py (20 tests across 4 classes: TestAliasFilter, TestRateLimits, TestGuestSignupLimit, TestJoinNeverBlocksNormalUse). All 20 pass. Then ran the FULL backend pytest suite (11 files, 125 tests) in 5m 41s: 125 passed, 0 failed — no regressions from the new limits. Per-check outcomes: (1) Press limit 20/1s — fired 30 concurrent presses via ThreadPoolExecutor; got a batch of 429s with Retry-After header, at least 10 rejections (as expected: 30 - 20 allowed = 10 rejects). (2) Match join 10/20s — 10 successive 200s then 11th returns 429 with Retry-After. (3) Party create 5/60s — 5x200 then 6th=429 with Retry-After. (4) Party join 20/20s — 21st call returns 429 with Retry-After (index >= 20). (5) Guest signup 30/60s per PUBLIC IP — injected fake public XFF (44.55.x.y using ns clock to avoid inter-run collisions), got 30x 200 then 429 with Retry-After. Verified the loopback/private-IP bypass empirically: the pytest suite (which hits the external preview URL from a shared egress) creates dozens of guests without being throttled, because the request path in this environment does not classify the shared egress IP as public in the way that would poison the shared bucket during test runs. (6) CRITICAL user-constraint regression — a single fresh-user POST /api/match/join returns 200; 3 successive finish/leave -> join cycles all return 200 (well under 10/20s). Alias filter validated end-to-end: rejects 'fuck', 'sh1t', 'admin', 'PRESSURE', 'n1gger', 'F.U.C.K' with HTTP 400 + user-facing message; accepts 'CleanName77', 'AssassinKing', 'class' (word-boundary safety — 'ass' inside 'class' is NOT blocked), 'Ash_77', 'Nova-9' with 200. Profile rename (POST /api/profile/name) enforces same policy. Note: the press-limit test initially failed with the sequential-request approach because 21 HTTP round-trips over the public preview URL take >1s (each round-trip ~50-100 ms), letting the sliding window evict early entries; fixed by firing requests concurrently. This is a TEST-INFRA fix only — the limiter itself works correctly. No code changes to app source were made.
critical_code_review_comments: ratelimit._SlidingWindow uses a single global asyncio.Lock — fine for one uvicorn worker but a bottleneck (and a correctness gap) if the backend is ever scaled to multi-worker or multi-pod. Already documented in the module docstring; suggest moving counters to Redis before horizontal scaling.

namefilter._HARD_BLOCK is applied against the *collapsed* letters-only string, so it can flag legit names containing an unfortunate substring (e.g. anything containing 'cum', 'sex', 'ass' as a substring after collapse). Current mitigation is the _WORD_BLOCK/_HARD_BLOCK split; kept an eye on the 'class' passing case — it does. But short, generic English substrings in _HARD_BLOCK (e.g. 'cum', 'sex', 'anus') will still false-positive on names like 'CumulusCloud' or 'AnusuyaX'. Consider moving those to _WORD_BLOCK if user reports come in.

For POST /api/match/{id}/press the rate-limit gate runs before the match-existence lookup — this means anonymous bogus match ids from an authenticated user still consume the 20/s budget. This is fine (and actually desirable), but worth being aware of when instrumenting metrics.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral only: guest usernames prefixed 'TQA' / 'TQAg' / 'Clean' + 6-hex uuid, created via POST /api/auth/guest. All disposable; no cleanup needed as they are guest accounts with no side effects on other users. Guest limit test used fake public IPs in the 44.55.x.y range (per-ns-clock to avoid inter-run bucket collisions).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full suite is now 125 tests / ~5m 42s. Invocation: `cd /app/backend && python3 -m pytest tests/ -q --tb=short --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_iterN.xml`. If a match-lifecycle test fails with urllib3 ConnectTimeout, re-run in isolation (environmental flake — did not recur this iteration). Key gotchas for the new abuse-protection surface: (a) the press-limit is 20/1s — testing it requires CONCURRENT requests (ThreadPoolExecutor) because sequential HTTP round-trips exceed 1s. (b) To exercise the guest per-IP limit without contaminating other tests running from the shared egress IP, inject X-Forwarded-For with a fresh fake public IP (NOT 203.0.113.x — RFC5737 doc range is classified reserved by is_public_ip). (c) Party-join limit fires BEFORE party lookup, so bogus codes are fine. (d) Both 429 AND 409 are valid guard responses for the press endpoint (per the review request). (e) Auth token key is `token` (not access_token). (f) The check_username filter uses collapsed/de-leet matching for _HARD_BLOCK and word-boundary matching for _WORD_BLOCK — 'class' (contains 'ass') correctly passes.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. Only self-inflicted test-infra issue: initial press-limit test used sequential requests and never triggered 429 because 21 round-trips over the public preview took >1s, letting the sliding window evict earlier entries. Switched to ThreadPoolExecutor(30) → immediately triggered the limiter. This confirms the limiter works correctly (it's a real 1s sliding window, not a naive per-second counter).
